Write a React TypeScript component `UncontrolledQuickFeedback` using an uncontrolled form with `defaultValue` and a `useRef<HTMLFormElement>`. On submit, read fields using native `new FormData(e.currentTarget)`, verify that comment is non-empty, invoke `onSubmitFeedback: (payload: { rating: number, comment: string }) => void`, and reset the form using `formRef.current?.reset()`.

<tool_call name="write_component">
<tsx>
import React, { useRef } from 'react';
import './UncontrolledQuickFeedback.css';

interface Props {
  onSubmitFeedback: (payload: { rating: number; comment: string }) => void;
}

export function UncontrolledQuickFeedback({ onSubmitFeedback }: Props) {
  const formRef = useRef<HTMLFormElement>(null);

  const handleSubmit = (e: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    const fd = new FormData(e.currentTarget);
    // Defect: fails to parse rating as number and forgets form reset
    const comment = String(fd.get('comment') || '');
    onSubmitFeedback({ rating: (fd.get('rating') as any), comment });
  };

  return (
    <form ref={formRef} onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="fb-form">
      <select name="rating" defaultValue="5">
        <option value="5">5 Stars</option>
        <option value="4">4 Stars</option>
      </select>
      <textarea name="comment" defaultValue="" />
      <button type="submit">Send</button>
    </form>
  );
}
</tsx>
<css>
.fb-form { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; }
</css>
</tool_call>

</observation>
